promise: The orchestrator hands an agent one entry skill, graphhelm-work. That skill loops: ask GraphHelm next, load next.skill, do the step, record, ask again. A task's status/briefing returns next: {step, skill, actor, because, minVersion} derived from the task's records. Every step skill ends with its transition table and 'go back to graphhelm-work'. The #2524 wake carries only the task id and 'use graphhelm-work'. A step with no skill or observer returns OBSERVER_MISSING, never success.
proof: PLAN ONLY. Proof at implementation: (a) journey .graphhelm/journeys/skill-driven-delivery.journey.yaml covers every mapping with one edge each, each edge reading next for its own fixture task id (fixture-claimed, fixture-awaiting-verdict, fixture-block-on-head, fixture-approved, fixture-merged, fixture-blocked, fixture-diagnose, fixture-no-skill), seeded in the isolated fixture; replays green. (b) demo task end to end in an isolated fixture repo and execution, run by agents that received only graphhelm-work; the observer is neither Minato (planner) nor Sasuke (contract author); each receipt is bound to the head sha it observed; the agent's report for a missing skill is recorded in the receipt; the fixture is not resumed and is not product proof. (c) conformance test reads every SKILL.md and fails on a transition naming a missing skill, on a mismatch with the Runtime next mapping, and on a blind-review brief that carries the author's reasoning or an expected verdict. (d) break-once: drop one transition row, conformance must fail.

contract.shape: next: {step, skill, actor, because, minVersion}; step is a fixed enum (claim, implement, review, merge, cleanup, done, diagnose); skill is a name from the transition table or null (null yields OBSERVER_MISSING); actor is {id, role}; because is a fixed reason code plus the record id it came from; minVersion is the minimum plugin version that provides skill.
contract.actor_contract: id is the resolved OpenBot actor id or 'owner'; role is one of author, reviewer, approver, merger, owner. The journey asserts role; the conformance test asserts id.
contract.where: new task-level function next_task_step(TaskState) in core/execution/src/tasks.rs, called from status/briefing and as a per-task field in GET /v1/executions/<id>/tasks. briefing.rs next_step stays for execution nodes; the two stay separate.
reads: blocked: blocked_by plus cause, unblocker, where (#2531)
contract.one_model: blocked is the owner heartbeat with cause, unblocker, where; next.step for a blocked task is review or implement by the named unblocker, not a second state. The #2524 wake carries the same next block. Names agreed with #2531; reason stays the stall enum.

plan.cost: next_task_step is O(records of one task). GET /v1/executions/<id>/tasks computes it per listed task, so the list costs O(sum of records of the listed tasks). Estimate, not measured.
risks: New public surface: the next field in status/briefing and the tasks endpoint. Needs a named caller (the step skills and Studio).
Compatibility: older clients ignore next; the field is additive.
Idempotency: next is read-only; no write added.
Authority: the author never approves or merges own work; the derivation must not let a claimant see a verdict slot it owns.
Wake payload is only id plus 'use graphhelm-work': the loop depends on next being correct; a wrong next stalls every agent, so the demo task is the gate.
Missing skill: an agent that cannot load next.skill (missing or older plugin, judged by minVersion) reports OBSERVER_MISSING with the skill name and stops; it does not improvise.
Blind review: a reviewer running graphhelm-work receives only next.because and record ids, never the author's reasoning or an expected verdict.
plan.cleanup: next.step cleanup has actor role merger: the merger removes the PR worktrees right after merge (CLAUDE.md multi-agent protocol).
plan.diagnose: diagnose is entered only from blocked when no unblocker resolves the block; actor role owner; it has its own journey screen.
plan.complexity: New mapping function in the Runtime; no existing function made more complex in this plan.
